fatal_errors: The proposed La(Fe,Si)13/Ce material is unrelated to the target Mn0.6Ni1−xSi0.62Fe0.4CoxGe0.38 high-entropy alloy system.
It fails to reconstruct the key intervention: systematic Co-for-Ni substitution from x = 0.40 to 0.55.
It misses the central result that increasing Co suppresses rather than improves the giant magnetocaloric response, reducing peak −ΔSM from 48.5 to 2.6 J kg−1 K−1 at 5 T.
The cited evidence concerns CoCrFeMnNi and AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys and provides no support for Fe/Si tuning or Ce substitution in La(Fe,Si)13.
No quantitative composition, processing protocol, transition temperatures, field conditions, or magnetocaloric performance values are provided.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses room-temperature magnetocaloric optimization in a broad sense and proposes a testable compositional series, but it does not match the target material, substitution strategy, processing, baseline, or observed trend. The target identifies the low-Co x = 0.40 Mn–Ni–Si–Fe–Co–Ge alloy as the strongest performer because its first-order hexagonal-to-orthorhombic transition is coupled to magnetic ordering near 306–309 K. Increasing Co stabilizes the hexagonal phase, lowers the transition temperatures, and eventually removes the first-order coupling at x = 0.55. Although the proposed XRD, magnetometry, calorimetry, and hysteresis measurements could discriminate its separate hypothesis, the supplied citations do not concern La(Fe,Si)13 and therefore cannot validate it.
